transcript.content: Hello, I'm Dr. Smith. It's nice to meet you. Could you please tell me what brings you in to see me today?

Hi, Dr. Smith. Nice to meet you too. Well, I guess what finally pushed me to come in is that my eating has just been all over the place lately. Some weeks I barely even touch dinner, and then other nights... I just find myself standing in the kitchen eating crackers and sweets after everyone else has gone to bed. I just realized I needed to talk to someone about it.
During those nights when you are eating the crackers and sweets, do you feel like you are unable to stop or control how much you are eating?

No, not really. I mean, it's not like I feel out of control or anything like that. I just... I get up, I eat a few things, and then I go back to bed. It's just more than I usually eat, but I don't feel like I can't stop.
Are you having any trouble falling asleep or staying asleep during the night?
No, my sleep has been fine. I don't really have any trouble falling asleep, and I usually stay asleep unless I wake up to get a snack, like I mentioned. But other than that, I sleep okay.
Over the past few weeks, have you felt a persistent sense of sadness or a loss of interest in the things you usually enjoy?

Yeah, I have. I go through these stretches where... I don't know, the whole house just feels gray and heavy. I'll just sit at the kitchen table feeling completely empty, even though nothing terrible has actually happened that day. It's just this lingering sadness that doesn't really have a reason.
Do you find that you spend a significant amount of your day worrying about various aspects of your life, such as work, finances, or your health?

No, not really. I mean, I guess I have normal concerns just like anyone else, but... no, I wouldn't say I spend a significant amount of time worrying about my health or money or anything like that. It doesn't really take up my day.
During those times when you feel that persistent sadness, have you noticed that your movements or speech seem much slower than usual, or conversely, that you feel restless and unable to sit still?

No, I haven't really noticed anything like that. I mean, I sit at the table a lot when I feel that way, but I don't think I'm moving or talking in slow motion. And I'm not restless, either. I don't have any trouble sitting still... I just kind of sit there. My body feels normal, I just feel sad.
Have you experienced similar periods of feeling this way in the past, perhaps months or years ago, or is this the first time you have ever felt this kind of sadness?

Yeah, I've felt this way in the past. It's definitely not the first time. If I really think about it... these gray, guilty periods where I just lose interest in things, they've probably added up to about seven months total.
Have you ever had periods where you felt unusually energetic, euphoric, or invincible, or where you felt you could go for days with very little sleep without feeling tired?

Yes, I have had times like that. There are periods when I just feel... bright, you know? Like I'm completely unstoppable and have all this energy. But then, almost out of nowhere, I can get suddenly furious over something really small. Like, if my husband moves my paints, or if he asks me about a receipt from the store, I just get so angry. It's like this intense high that can turn into being really irritated very quickly.
During those times when you feel that bright, unstoppable energy, how many days in a row does that feeling typically last?

I'm not really sure, to be honest. I've never actually counted the days when it's happening. It just kind of... goes on for a while until it eventually stops. I've never really paid attention to an exact number of days.

During those times when you feel that 'bright' energy, does it become so intense that it causes major problems in your work or your relationships, or have you ever had to be hospitalized because of it?

No, it doesn't really get to that point. I mean, the irritation with my husband can cause some arguments, but it's never caused major problems or gotten me fired from a job or anything like that. And I've never been hospitalized for it, no. It's just... a lot of energy, but not out of control like that.
When you have these periods of feeling bright and unstoppable, do they consistently last for at least four days in a row?

I really couldn't say for certain. Like I mentioned a minute ago, I just don't track it. It... it might be four days, or maybe a few days, but I've never marked it on a calendar or anything to see exactly how long it is. I just know it lasts for a stretch of time, but I don't know if it's consistently four days in a row.
During those 'bright' periods, have other people, like your husband or friends, ever remarked that you were acting noticeably different from your usual self?

I'm not really sure. My husband hasn't ever said anything like that to me. I mean, he obviously notices when I'm more irritable and we end up arguing, but he's never actually remarked that I'm acting noticeably different from my normal self. And I don't really see friends often enough for them to comment on it. So... no, no one has really pointed it out to me.
